import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Rectilinear crossing number and halving lines

Let $S$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane in general position (no three collinear).
The straight-line drawing of the complete graph $K_n$ on $S$ has a *crossing* for each
unordered pair of edges whose relative interiors meet. The *rectilinear crossing number*
$\overline{cr}(n)$ is the minimum number of crossings over all such $S$.

A *halving line* of $S$ is a line through two points of $S$ that equally bisects the
remaining points, i.e. has the same number of points of $S$ strictly on each side.

The conjecture states that every $n$-point set in general position that minimizes the
number of crossings also maximizes the number of halving lines.
(The converse is known to fail: some sets maximizing the number of halving lines have a
quadrilateral as convex hull, whereas all sets minimizing the number of crossings have a
triangular convex hull.)

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Wikipedia, Crossing number (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/crossing_number_%28graph_theory%29)
* [Rectilinear Crossing Number project](http://www.ist.tugraz.at/staff/aichholzer/research/rp/triangulations/crossing/)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry Finset

namespace CrossingNumber

/-- The number of crossings of the straight-line drawing of the complete graph on the vertex
set `S`: the number of unordered pairs of distinct edges (segments between two points of `S`)
whose relative interiors meet. -/
noncomputable def rectilinearCrossings (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  {E : Sym2 (Sym2 ℝ²) | ¬ E.IsDiag ∧
    ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, ∃ c ∈ S, ∃ d ∈ S, a ≠ b ∧ c ≠ d ∧
      E = s(s(a, b), s(c, d)) ∧ (openSegment ℝ a b ∩ openSegment ℝ c d).Nonempty}.ncard

open scoped Classical in
/-- The affine subspace `L` (a line) *equally bisects* the finite point set `S` if, for every
point `c ∈ S` not on `L`, the points of `S` strictly on the same side of `L` as `c` are as
many as the points of `S` strictly on the opposite side. -/
def Bisects (L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) (S : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ S, c ∉ L → #{p ∈ S | L.SSameSide c p} = #{p ∈ S | L.SOppSide c p}

/-- The halving lines of `S`: the lines through two points of `S` that equally bisect the
remaining points of `S`. -/
def halvingLines (S : Finset ℝ²) : Set (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) :=
  {L | ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, a ≠ b ∧ L = line[ℝ, a, b] ∧ Bisects L S}

/-- The number of halving lines of `S`. -/
noncomputable def numHalvingLines (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  (halvingLines S).ncard

@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem rectilinearCrossings_empty : rectilinearCrossings ∅ = 0 := by
  simp [rectilinearCrossings]

@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem numHalvingLines_empty : numHalvingLines ∅ = 0 := by
  simp [numHalvingLines, halvingLines]

/-- Two distinct points have exactly one halving line: the line through them. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem numHalvingLines_pair (a b : ℝ²) (hab : a ≠ b) : numHalvingLines {a, b} = 1 := by
  unfold numHalvingLines
  rw [Set.ncard_eq_one]
  refine ⟨line[ℝ, a, b], ?_⟩
  ext L
  simp only [halvingLines, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff, mem_insert, mem_singleton]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, y, hy, hxy, rfl, -⟩
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy with rfl | rfl
    · exact absurd rfl hxy
    · rfl
    · exact Set.pair_comm _ _ ▸ rfl
    · exact absurd rfl hxy
  · rintro rfl
    refine ⟨a, by simp, b, by simp, hab, rfl, ?_⟩
    intro c hc hcL
    simp only [mem_insert, mem_singleton] at hc
    rcases hc with rfl | rfl
    · exact absurd (left_mem_affineSpan_pair ℝ c b) hcL
    · exact absurd (right_mem_affineSpan_pair ℝ a c) hcL

/-- The point set `S` is in general position (no three points collinear) and minimizes the
rectilinear crossing number: no point set of the same size in general position has fewer
crossings. -/
def MinimizesCrossings (S : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  NonTrilinear (S : Set ℝ²) ∧
    ∀ T : Finset ℝ², #T = #S → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) →
      rectilinearCrossings S ≤ rectilinearCrossings T

/-- The point set `S` is in general position (no three points collinear) and maximizes the
number of halving lines: no point set of the same size in general position has more halving
lines. -/
def MaximizesHalvingLines (S : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  NonTrilinear (S : Set ℝ²) ∧
    ∀ T : Finset ℝ², #T = #S → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) →
      numHalvingLines T ≤ numHalvingLines S

/--
For each arrangement of points in which the rectilinear crossing number is minimized,
is the number of halving lines maximized?

That is: for every $n$ and every set $S$ of $n$ points in the plane in general position
such that the straight-line drawing of $K_n$ on $S$ has the minimum number of crossings
among all such $n$-point sets, does $S$ have the maximum number of halving lines among all
such $n$-point sets?

For odd $n$ no line through two points of $S$ can equally bisect the remaining $n - 2$
points, so both sides of the comparison are $0$ and the question is only of interest for
even $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossing_number : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ S : Finset ℝ², MinimizesCrossings S → MaximizesHalvingLines S := by
  sorry

end CrossingNumber

modeling_decisions: Point sets are `Finset ℝ²` (ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), the repo's scoped notation) in general position, expressed with the repo's `EuclideanGeometry.NonTrilinear` (no three collinear). General position is required both for S and for the comparison sets T, since the rectilinear crossing number of K_n is a minimum over straight-line drawings, which for K_n forces no three collinear vertices.

'The rectilinear crossing number is minimized' is rendered as: S is in general position and `rectilinearCrossings S ≤ rectilinearCrossings T` for every general-position T with `#T = #S` (equivalently cr(S) = cr̄(n)). This avoids sInf/sSup defaults; 'number of halving lines is maximized' is rendered symmetrically with ≥. The implicit quantifier over n is realised by quantifying over all finite S and comparing with sets of the same cardinality.

Crossings are counted literally as unordered pairs of distinct edges (`Sym2 (Sym2 ℝ²)` with `¬ E.IsDiag`) spanned by points of S whose relative interiors `openSegment ℝ a b`, `openSegment ℝ c d` intersect; the count is `Set.ncard`. Using open segments means edges sharing an endpoint do not cross (in general position), and concurrent crossings are counted per pair of edges, matching the standard definition. I deliberately did not use the equivalent 'number of convex quadrilaterals' characterisation, to stay with the source's definition.

A halving line is a line `line[ℝ, a, b]` through two distinct points of S that `Bisects` S: for every c ∈ S off the line, #{p ∈ S | SSameSide c p} = #{p ∈ S | SOppSide c p} (Mathlib's strict same/opposite side predicates; c is counted on its own side via `sSameSide_self_iff`). The ∀ c formulation makes the two-point case (no remaining points) correctly a halving line and is equivalent to any fixed-witness formulation when remaining points exist. Halving lines are counted as a set of affine subspaces (`Set.ncard`), literally 'number of halving lines'; in general position this equals the number of qualifying pairs.
The statement is phrased as a yes/no question in the source, so it uses `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`; `answer(True)` is the positive answer that the article records as the conjecture.

All n are quantified (no restriction to even n). For odd n no line can equally bisect n−2 points, so both counts are 0 and the implication is trivially true; this is documented in the theorem docstring and makes the statement logically equivalent to the even-n restriction used by some sources.

The article's remark that the converse fails (halving-line maximizers with quadrilateral convex hull) is recorded only in the module docstring as background, not as a declaration, per the decomposition notes.
Three `@[category test]` lemmas with proofs check the bespoke definitions on boundary inputs: empty set has 0 crossings and 0 halving lines; two distinct points have exactly one halving line.

namespace CrossingNumber

open EuclideanGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- The number of crossings in the straight-line drawing of the complete graph on `P`.
For points with no three collinear, each crossing corresponds to a unique four-point subset in
convex position. -/
def rectilinearCrossingCount (P : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (P.powersetCard 4 |>.filter fun (Q : Finset ℝ²) ↦ ConvexIndep (Q : Set ℝ²)).card

/-- A two-point subset `L` of `P` determines a halving line if the two open half-planes bounded by
that line contain the same number of points of `P`. -/
def IsHalvingLine (P L : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ a ∈ L, ∃ b ∈ L, a ≠ b ∧
    (P.filter fun x ↦ 0 < triangle_area a b x).card =
      (P.filter fun x ↦ triangle_area a b x < 0).card

/-- The number of halving lines determined by pairs of points of `P`. -/
def halvingLineCount (P : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (P.powersetCard 2 |>.filter (IsHalvingLine P)).card

/--
For every $n$ and every $n$-point set $P$ in the plane with no three points collinear, if the
straight-line drawing of $K_n$ on $P$ has the minimum number of crossings among all such
$n$-point sets, then $P$ has the maximum number of halving lines among all such sets. A halving
line passes through two points of $P$ and has equally many of the remaining points in each open
half-plane.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem crossing_number : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (P : Finset ℝ²), P.card = n → NonTrilinear (P : Set ℝ²) →
      (∀ Q : Finset ℝ², Q.card = n → NonTrilinear (Q : Set ℝ²) →
        rectilinearCrossingCount P ≤ rectilinearCrossingCount Q) →
      ∀ Q : Finset ℝ², Q.card = n → NonTrilinear (Q : Set ℝ²) →
        halvingLineCount Q ≤ halvingLineCount P := by
  sorry

end

end CrossingNumber
modeling_decisions: Modeled an arrangement as a finite set `P : Finset ℝ²`, so points are intrinsically distinct; quantified over every natural number `n`, including odd `n`.

Interpreted the implicit general-position condition as exactly no three points collinear, using `EuclideanGeometry.NonTrilinear`; did not use the repository's stronger `InGeneralPosition`, which additionally forbids four concyclic points.

Counted crossings in the straight-line drawing of `K_n` by convex-independent four-point subsets. Under the no-three-collinear hypothesis, each such subset determines exactly one crossing pair of edges, matching the article's convention of counting separately for each pair of crossing edges even if several edges cross at one location.

Represented a halving line by an unordered two-point `Finset`. The signs of `EuclideanGeometry.triangle_area` identify its two open half-planes; equality of the two filtered cardinalities expresses equal bisection of all remaining points.

Expressed minimum and maximum relationally over all general-position point sets of the same cardinality, rather than introducing extrema with default values. Thus the hypothesis says the given arrangement attains the minimum crossing count, and the conclusion says it attains the maximum halving-line count.

Used `answer(sorry) ↔` around the positive universal proposition because the source poses a yes/no question and the article identifies the positive answer as the conjecture. For odd `n`, no two-point line can split the odd number `n - 2` of remaining points equally, so the resulting maximum count is literally zero.

/-!
# Rectilinear crossing number and halving lines

Let $S$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane in general position (no three collinear). Draw the
complete graph $K_n$ with vertex set $S$ and straight-line edges. The number of crossings of this
drawing is the number of pairs of edges that cross. The *rectilinear crossing number*
$\overline{cr}(n)$ of $K_n$ is the minimum of this number over all such $S$.

A *halving line* of $S$ is a line through two points of $S$ that equally bisects the remaining
$n - 2$ points, i.e. has $(n - 2)/2$ of them on each side.

It is conjectured that for each arrangement of points for which $\overline{cr}(n)$ is minimized,
the number of halving lines is maximized.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Crossing number (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/crossing_number_%28graph_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry Finset

namespace CrossingNumber

open scoped Classical in
/--
The number of crossings of the straight-line drawing of the complete graph with vertex set `S`.
The edges of the drawing are the segments joining two distinct points of `S`. Two edges cross when
their open segments meet. `crossings S` is the number of unordered pairs of distinct edges that
cross.
-/
noncomputable def crossings (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  #{P ∈ (S.powersetCard 2).powersetCard 2 |
    ∃ a b c d, P = {{a, b}, {c, d}} ∧ (openSegment ℝ a b ∩ openSegment ℝ c d).Nonempty}

/--
The line through the points `a` and `b` is a halving line of `S` if the points of `S` strictly on
one side of it are as many as the points of `S` strictly on the other side. The side of a point
`c` is given by the sign of the signed area `triangle_area a b c` of the triangle `a b c`.
-/
def IsHalvingLine (S : Finset ℝ²) (a b : ℝ²) : Prop :=
  #{c ∈ S | 0 < triangle_area a b c} = #{c ∈ S | triangle_area a b c < 0}

/-- The number of halving lines of `S`: the number of lines through two distinct points of `S`
that equally bisect the remaining points of `S`. -/
noncomputable def halvingLines (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  {ℓ : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ² | ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, a ≠ b ∧ ℓ = line[ℝ, a, b] ∧ IsHalvingLine S a b}.ncard

/--
**Rectilinear crossing number and halving lines.**

Let $S$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane in general position (no three collinear) whose
straight-line drawing of $K_n$ has the minimum number of crossings among all such $n$-point sets,
i.e. an arrangement of points for which the rectilinear crossing number $\overline{cr}(n)$ is
attained. Is the number of halving lines of $S$ then maximal among all $n$-point sets in general
position?

The conjecture asserts the positive answer. For odd $n$ no set in general position has a halving
line, so the question is only of interest for even $n$. The converse is known to be false.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossing_number :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ S : Finset ℝ², NonTrilinear (S : Set ℝ²) →
      (∀ T : Finset ℝ², #T = #S → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) → crossings S ≤ crossings T) →
      ∀ T : Finset ℝ², #T = #S → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) → halvingLines T ≤ halvingLines S := by
  sorry

/-- The empty drawing has no crossings. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossings_empty : crossings ∅ = 0 := by
  rw [crossings, Finset.powersetCard_eq_empty.mpr (by simp)]
  simp

/-- The vertices $(0,0), (2,0), (1,1), (1,-1)$ of a convex quadrilateral give one crossing: the two
diagonals $(0,0)(2,0)$ and $(1,1)(1,-1)$ cross. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossings_convex_quadrilateral :
    crossings {!₂[0, 0], !₂[2, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[1, -1]} = 1 := by
  sorry

/-- The diagonal $(0,0)(2,0)$ of the convex quadrilateral $(0,0), (1,-1), (2,0), (1,1)$ is a
halving line: $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$ lie on opposite sides of it. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem isHalvingLine_diagonal :
    IsHalvingLine {!₂[0, 0], !₂[2, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[1, -1]} !₂[0, 0] !₂[2, 0] := by
  simp [IsHalvingLine, triangle_area_eq_det, Matrix.det_fin_three, Finset.filter_insert,
    Finset.filter_singleton]
  norm_num

/-- The side $(0,0)(1,1)$ of the convex quadrilateral $(0,0), (1,-1), (2,0), (1,1)$ is not a
halving line: $(2,0)$ and $(1,-1)$ lie on the same side of it. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem not_isHalvingLine_side :
    ¬ IsHalvingLine {!₂[0, 0], !₂[2, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[1, -1]} !₂[0, 0] !₂[1, 1] := by
  simp [IsHalvingLine, triangle_area_eq_det, Matrix.det_fin_three, Finset.filter_insert,
    Finset.filter_singleton]
  norm_num

end CrossingNumber

namespace CrossingNumber

/-- The four-element set `T` carries a crossing of the straight-line drawing of the complete
graph on `T`: `T = {a, b, c, d}` and the open segments `ab` and `cd` meet.

For a point set with no three points collinear, two spanned segments can only cross if their
four endpoints are distinct, and a four-point set carries at most one crossing pair (the two
diagonals of a convex quadrilateral). So the number of crossings of the straight-line drawing of
$K_n$ on such a set equals the number of its four-element subsets satisfying `HasCrossing`. -/
def HasCrossing (T : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c d, T = {a, b, c, d} ∧ (openSegment ℝ a b ∩ openSegment ℝ c d).Nonempty

/-- The number of crossings of the straight-line drawing of the complete graph with vertex
set `S`, that is, the number of four-element subsets of `S` carrying a crossing. -/
noncomputable def crossingCount (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  #{T ∈ S.powersetCard 4 | HasCrossing T}

/-- The line through `a` and `b` equally bisects `S`: the number of points of `S` strictly on
one side of the line equals the number of points of `S` strictly on the other side. The two sides
are distinguished by the sign of the signed area `triangle_area a b c`. -/
def IsHalvingLine (S : Finset ℝ²) (a b : ℝ²) : Prop :=
  #{c ∈ S | 0 < triangle_area a b c} = #{c ∈ S | triangle_area a b c < 0}

the number of halving lines of `S`. -/

# Crossing number

This file states a conjectured relation between crossing-minimal straight-line drawings of
complete graphs and point sets with the maximum number of halving lines.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Crossing number (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/crossing_number_%28graph_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry
open EuclideanGeometry

namespace CrossingNumber

/-- Two straight edges cross properly when their open segments intersect. The arguments are
unordered endpoint sets. -/
def SegmentsCross (e f : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c d : ℝ², e = {a, b} ∧ f = {c, d} ∧
    (openSegment ℝ a b ∩ openSegment ℝ c d).Nonempty

/-- The number of crossings in the straight-line drawing of the complete graph on `P`.
Each crossing pair of edges is counted once. -/
noncomputable def rectilinearCrossingCount (P : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  let edges := P.powersetCard 2
  ((edges.powersetCard 2).filter fun E ↦
    ∃ e ∈ E, ∃ f ∈ E, e ≠ f ∧ SegmentsCross e f).card

/-- The signed side of `p` relative to the directed line from `a` to `b`. Its sign distinguishes
the two open half-planes bounded by that line. -/
def sideValue (a b p : ℝ²) : ℝ :=
  (b 0 - a 0) * (p 1 - a 1) - (b 1 - a 1) * (p 0 - a 0)

/-- The number of lines through two points of `P` which leave equally many of the other points
in each of their two open half-planes. -/
noncomputable def halvingLineCount (P : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  ((P.powersetCard 2).filter fun e ↦
    ∃ a ∈ e, ∃ b ∈ e, a ≠ b ∧
      (P.filter fun p ↦ 0 < sideValue a b p).card =
        (P.filter fun p ↦ sideValue a b p < 0).card).card

/--
For every `n` and every `n`-point set in general position (no three points collinear), if its
straight-line drawing of $K_n$ has the minimum possible number of crossings among all such
`n`-point sets, must its number of halving lines be the maximum possible among all such sets?
A halving line passes through two points and has equally many remaining points in each open
half-plane. Thus, under this literal definition, odd-cardinality sets have no halving lines.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossing_number : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Finset ℝ²), S.card = n → NonTrilinear (S : Set ℝ²) →
      (∀ T : Finset ℝ², T.card = n → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) →
        rectilinearCrossingCount S ≤ rectilinearCrossingCount T) →
      ∀ T : Finset ℝ², T.card = n → NonTrilinear (T : Set ℝ²) →
        halvingLineCount T ≤ halvingLineCount S := by
  sorry

end CrossingNumber

Defined an arrangement's straight-line crossing count directly as the number of unordered pairs of two-point edges whose open segments intersect. This counts each crossing edge-pair once and excludes intersections at shared endpoints.

open EuclideanGeometry

are split equally between the two open half-planes bounded by their line. -/
def IsHalvingPair (S e : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  e ⊆ S ∧ e.card = 2 ∧
    ∃ a ∈ e, ∃ b ∈ e, a ≠ b ∧
      ((S \ e).filter fun c ↦ 0 < triangle_area a b c).card =
        ((S \ e).filter fun c ↦ triangle_area a b c < 0).card

/-- The number of halving lines determined by `S`. Each line is represented by its
unordered pair of incident points. -/
noncomputable def halvingLineCount (S : Finset ℝ²) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (S.powerset.filter fun e ↦ IsHalvingPair S e).card

point set `S` in general position. It is the number of four-point subsets of `S` in
convex position. -/

    Q.card = 4 ∧ ConvexIndep (Q : Set ℝ²)).card

minimizes the rectilinear crossing number among all such sets also maximize the number

        ((S \ L).filter fun p ↦ (∡ a b p).sign = -1).card
